_comment: Plot settings, native emtk window. 'settings' is the scrolling form (one collapsible panel per section of the Qt tool), 'actions' the Apply / Save / Reset bar, 'preview' the sample plot docked beside it (drawn by gui/app.py: a plot is not something a spec can express). Drawn by emtk.view_form over PlotSettingsModel (gui/model.py).
title: Plot Settings

sections.name: settings
sections.title: Settings
sections.description: All plot settings.

sections.title: Rendering Backend
sections.description: Which engine draws newly created plots.

sections.label: Active backend
sections.description: Rendering backend for chiplot panels: emtk is the native renderer, pyqtgraph the legacy one. It is used by plots created after you apply the change.

sections.text: Changes apply on next application start or when a new plot is created.
sections.description: When a changed backend takes effect.

sections.title: Colors
sections.description: The palette curves and regions take in every plot. The preview below follows the edits.

sections.label: Data curve
sections.description: Colour of the data curve in decay plots. Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value such as #ffa52f.

sections.label: Model curve
sections.description: Colour of the fitted model curve. Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value.

sections.label: Instrument response
sections.description: Colour of the instrument response function (IRF). Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value.

sections.label: Residuals
sections.description: Colour of the weighted residuals panel. Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value.

sections.label: Autocorrelation
sections.description: Colour of the autocorrelation curve. Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value.

sections.label: Region selector
sections.description: Colour of the draggable fit-range band. Click the swatch for a colour picker, or type a hex value.

sections.label: Region alpha
sections.description: Opacity of the fit-range band, 0 (invisible) to 255 (solid).

sections.label: Active transparency
sections.description: Opacity of the active plot, 0 to 1.

sections.label: Inactive transparency
sections.description: Opacity of plots that are not active, 0 to 1.

sections.title: Appearance
sections.description: Line width, fonts, grid and which furniture the plots show.

sections.label: Line width
sections.description: Width of the data and model curves, 0.5 to 10 pixels.

sections.label: Axis font size
sections.description: Base point size for ticks, axis labels and titles. 'auto' (0) follows the application font.

sections.label: Grid opacity
sections.description: Grid line opacity, per cent.

sections.title: Options
sections.description: Which plot furniture is shown by default.

sections.label: Enable grid
sections.description: Show grid lines in the plots.

sections.label: Grid on data panel
sections.description: Draw the grid on the data (decay) panel.

sections.label: Grid on residuals
sections.description: Draw the grid on the residuals panel.

sections.label: Grid on autocorrelation
sections.description: Draw the grid on the autocorrelation panel.

sections.label: Fit-range selector
sections.description: Draw the draggable fit-range band on the data panel.

sections.label: Show legend by default
sections.description: Show the legend in new plots.

sections.label: Hide titles
sections.description: Hide plot titles by default.

sections.label: Label axes
sections.description: Show the axis names (counts, t / ns, ...).

sections.title: Node Graphs (Global View)
sections.description: Background grid and node size of the node graphs.

sections.label: Show grid
sections.description: Show the background grid of a node graph.

sections.label: Grid line width
sections.description: Grid line thickness. Below one pixel draws a hairline; on a HiDPI screen a full pixel doubles to two device pixels and the grid starts to out-weigh the edges drawn on top of it.

sections.label: Grid opacity
sections.description: Grid line opacity of a node graph, per cent.

sections.label: Grid spacing
sections.description: Distance between the grid lines of a node graph, 4 to 96 pixels.

sections.label: Node size (Global View)
sections.description: The node radius a newly opened Global View starts its own node-size control at. A window that is already open keeps the value its slider holds.

sections.text: Grid and spacing apply to Global View, the light path, the provenance inspector and the node editor; Apply also catches up the windows that are open.
sections.description: Where the node-graph settings take effect.

sections.title: Advanced: pyqtgraph Configuration
sections.description: Options that only exist on the pyqtgraph engine.

sections.label: Antialiasing
sections.description: Use antialiased lines in pyqtgraph plots.

sections.label: Left button pans
sections.description: Pan pyqtgraph plots with the left mouse button.

sections.label: Background
sections.description: pyqtgraph background colour: k black, w white, default the library default. The preview follows it.

sections.label: Foreground
sections.description: Axis, tick and label colour (d light grey, w white, l light, k black). Keep it contrasting with the background: matching the two hides every axis.

sections.name: actions
sections.title: Actions
sections.description: Apply, save or reload the plot settings.
Apply the edits, save them, or reload the active settings.

buttons.label: Apply
buttons.description: Write the edits into the active plot settings; plots created from now on use them, and open node graphs are re-styled.

buttons.label: Save
buttons.description: Apply the edits and write them to settings_chisurf.yaml so they are kept for the next start.

buttons.label: Reset
buttons.description: Reload every control from the active settings, discarding edits that were not applied.

sections.description: What the last action did, and whether edits are waiting to be applied.

sections.name: preview
sections.title: Preview (sample curves)
sections.description: A sample plot that previews the styling.
Sample curves (data, model, IRF) drawn with the colours, line width, grid, legend and background chosen on the left. They preview the styling and are not analysis data.
